title: CostFlow guardrails: SLO-aware routing, limiter profiles, and safe rollback orchestration
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Implement an end-to-end guardrail layer for CostFlow recommendations that enforces latency and throughput SLOs during automated batching/caching config changes. This ticket delivers: (1) SLO-aware routing decisions for optimization deploys, (2) limiter profile platform primitives (rate/batch/kv-cache caps) with staged apply semantics, (3) anomaly detection hooks to block/rollback unsafe changes, and (4) an automated safe-rollback orchestration with canary and recovery playbooks.

Scope and goals:
- Prevent cost-driven batching or cache configs from violating 95th/99th latency SLOs and throughput targets for customer routes.
- Make optimizer actions reversible and observable with minimal manual intervention.
- Integrate with Console for per-route dry-run, canary % selection, and rollback actions.

Core design decisions (high level):
- SLO evaluator: runtime-side SLO evaluator computes per-route rolling windows (1m/5m/30m) for p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput (rps) delta against baseline. Routing decisions consult the evaluator before applying config changes.
- Limiter profiles: define immutable profiles for BatchSize, MaxInflight, KVCacheTTL, and EffectiveConcurrency. Profiles express safe bounds (soft and hard caps). Optimizer proposals map to profiles; runtime enforces hard caps.
- Canary & staged apply: changes are first applied to a small percentage of traffic (configurable: 0.5%/1%/5%). Canary window uses a stricter SLO threshold (e.g., 0.8x latency slack). If anomalies are detected, the system automatically pauses and rolls back to previous profile.
- Anomaly detection: hybrid approach using statistical change detection (CUSUM) and simple rule-based triggers (latency increase > 30% p95 over baseline OR error rate spike > 0.5%). Alerts feed into the rollback controller.
- Safe rollback orchestration: the rollback controller runs deterministic multi-step rollback (pause optimizer, revert profile, incremental traffic shift back, and post-mortem ticket template).

Telemetry and observability:
- New Grafana dashboard: CostFlow Guardrails (per-route SLO deltas, canary cohorts, limiter saturation, rollback events).
- Events emitted to tracing and metrics backend with tags: optimizer_id, profile_id, cohort, rollback_reason.
- Dry-run endpoint to simulate optimizer suggestions and project expected SLO delta under historic traffic.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime rejects optimizer-applied profile if it exceeds hard caps for any route.
- Canary flow can be configured per-route and can be aborted automatically when anomaly detectors fire.
- Rollback controller completes a full automated rollback within configured SLA (target: full revert within 30s of anomaly detection for canary cohorts).
- Console shows canary status, can abort/advance canary, and exposes dry-run output for any proposed profile.
- E2E load tests demonstrating no more than 5% of customer routes experience p95 latency degradation > 20% during staged applies in the test harness.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Conservative hard caps reduce cost savings but increase safety. We bias towards conservative default profiles for P0 customers and make aggressive profiles opt-in.
- Detection sensitivity tuning: false positives cause unnecessary rollbacks; false negatives risk SLO breaches. We'll run a two-week tuning window with user traffic and synthetic stress tests.
- Coordination with Dedicated/Private deployments: limited telemetry surface may require local adapter hooks; document integration points in the private deployment guide.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/CostFlow+Guardrails
- Dry-run API spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/costflow/blob/main/docs/dry_run.md
- Draft Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/costflow-guardrails
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

Operational playbook (short):
- If an automated rollback occurs, the system will open a post-mortem ticket with pre-filled diagnostics (cohort metrics, PR, applied profile).
- On repeated rollbacks (>3 within 24h for same route), automatically disable optimizer writes for that route and create a manual review ticket.

Next steps / plan:
1) Implement limiter profile primitives (runtime + API) — 2 devs — 2 sprints.
2) Build SLO evaluator and routing integration — 2 devs — 1 sprint.
3) Canary flow, anomaly detectors, and rollback controller — 3 devs — 2 sprints.
4) Console UX: canary controls, dry-run UI, and dashboard — 1 frontend dev + 1 PM — 2 sprints.
5) Gradual rollouts and tuning on internal clusters, then small set of customers as beta.

Measure of success:
- 20% reduction in per-token serving cost for routes that adopt conservative profiles within 60 days, with no customer SLO regressions (customer_impact: none/low).
- <1 automated false-positive rollback per 100 optimizer applies after tuning.

Owner notes: coordinate with SRE (Riley Morgan) for alerting thresholds and with PM (Jin Park) for beta customer selection.
updates: 2026-03-03 — Kickoff: architecture and scope agreed with SRE and Runtime teams. Action items: limiter schema, evaluator API, canary config schema.
2026-03-05 — Prototype limiter profiles implemented in the local runtime branch. Basic validation added to API (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321).
2026-03-08 — First synthetic load test flagged a p95 spike when BatchSize increased beyond profile soft cap; tuned default soft caps down 15%.
2026-03-10 — Anomaly detection design reviewed with ML Infra; decided on CUSUM + simple threshold hybrid. Added plan for weekly tuning job using historical traffic windows.
2026-03-12 — Console UX wireframes uploaded to Confluence; included canary slider options (0.1%/0.5%/1%/5%).
2026-03-14 — Beta customer shortlist approved by PM. Scheduled private deployment adapter work for dedicated customers with restricted telemetry (ENG-28100).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime enforces profile hard caps and rejects any optimizer change exceeding them.
Canary apply completes a pass/fail evaluation using SLO evaluator and anomaly detectors within the configured window.
Automated rollback finishes reverting config and shifting traffic back within target SLA for canary cohorts.
Console exposes dry-run results and canary controls for operators.
E2E tests show SLO regressions remain within agreed thresholds under staged apply scenarios.
